abstract: Intermolecular G-quadruplexes (Inter-G4s) are implicated in long-range nucleic acid interactions, transcriptional regulation, and phase separation, yet how RNA/DNA strand composition shapes their mechanical stability and folding behavior remains poorly understood. Heterotypic RNA-DNA (R-D) Inter-G4s are particularly difficult to resolve because ensemble measurements cannot readily distinguish them from coexisting RNA-RNA (R-R) and DNA-DNA (D-D) assemblies. We developed Inter-GDP, a single-molecule platform that tethers two G-rich strands within one DNA construct, enabling repeated Inter-G4 folding and unfolding measurements. We established the platform using CSB II and two additional G4-forming sequences derived from structurally resolved bimolecular DNA G4s. Across three sequence contexts, the mean unfolding force followed the same ordering, R-R > D-D > R-D. BG4 responses were sequence- and construct-dependent, with reduced mean unfolding forces observed for Inter-G4 constructs associated with parallel bulk CD signatures. Simulations of a D-D Inter-G4 model suggested local conformational remodeling and lower G-quartet-core hydrogen-bond counts in BG4-containing trajectories. Together, our work establishes Inter-GDP as a single-molecule method for quantitative analysis of Inter-G4 mechanical stability and protein-associated effects.
